</li>
<li>
<strong>Main drivers:</strong>

Oysters, as sold from water-soluble had TMA higher at 6,150 µg/kg, against 430 µg/kg for lipid-soluble in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/kaise1988-marine-organisms-arsenic-speciation|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Kaise T, Hanaoka K, Tagawa S, Hirayama T, Fukui S · 1988</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/kaise1988-marine-organisms-arsenic-speciation">Distribution of inorganic arsenic and methylated arsenic in marine organisms</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Applied Organometallic Chemistry</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/kaise1988-marine-organisms-arsenic-speciation">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</li>
<li>
<strong>Practical framing:</strong>

Ask for lot results with a quantification limit well below the limit that applies in the destination market.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/barchiesi2020-shellfish-metals-central-italy|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Barchiesi F, Branciari R, Latini M, Roila R, Lediani G, Filippini G, Scortichini G, Piersanti A, Rocchegiani E, Ranucci D · 2020</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/barchiesi2020-shellfish-metals-central-italy">Heavy Metals Contamination in Shellfish: Benefit-Risk Evaluation in Central Italy</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Foods</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/barchiesi2020-shellfish-metals-central-italy">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/lehel2018-hungary-seafood-metals|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Lehel J, Bartha A, Danko D, Lanyi K, Laczay P · 2018</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/lehel2018-hungary-seafood-metals">Heavy metals in seafood purchased from a fishery market in Hungary</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food Additives &amp; Oysters, as sold from water-soluble had TMA higher at 6,150 µg/kg, against 430 µg/kg for lipid-soluble in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/kaise1988-marine-organisms-arsenic-speciation|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Kaise T, Hanaoka K, Tagawa S, Hirayama T, Fukui S · 1988</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/kaise1988-marine-organisms-arsenic-speciation">Distribution of inorganic arsenic and methylated arsenic in marine organisms</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Applied Organometallic Chemistry</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/kaise1988-marine-organisms-arsenic-speciation">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

For a buyer the practical points are the form bought, the basis a result is reported on, where the oysters came from and the laboratory’s reporting limit. Testing finds contamination but does not remove it.

<div class="hmi-analyte-explorer" id="hmi-occurrence-oyster" data-analyte-explorer data-compact-intro="true" data-source-summaries="true"><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-explorer-context><summary data-open-context aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-controls="hmi-occurrence-oyster-drawer">Comparison methods and scope</summary><div data-explorer-context-content>

<p>Each row is one statistic a source reports for one form of oysters, group and metal; percentiles, ranges and maxima reported for the same samples as a mean or median are shown on that row. Different forms and preparation states are kept apart, and dry-weight results never share a reference with as-sold or fresh-weight results. Ratings place a result against an HMI reference built from monitoring results and ordinary-setting medians for the same form and basis. Same-study contrasts compare a contaminated or treated site with its control, targeted with random sampling, a prepared form with the unprocessed one, or one group of a study with the median of its other groups. Held rows failed a check against their own source and are shown but not compared.</p>

At least four reference units and a definitely positive Q1 to Q3 spread are required. This is a display eligibility rule, not statistical validation.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Limitations</p><p>3 sampling families with different designs; none is a probability sample of world supply. <a id="sources-and-contamination-pathways"></a>
## How metals reach oysters

<a id="hmi-ing-010"></a>

<a id="hmi-ing-011"></a>

The evidence on how metals reach oysters comes from studies that compared exposed and ordinary settings. Oysters, as sold from water-soluble had TMA higher at 6,150 µg/kg, against 430 µg/kg for lipid-soluble in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/kaise1988-marine-organisms-arsenic-speciation|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Kaise T, Hanaoka K, Tagawa S, Hirayama T, Fukui S · 1988</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/kaise1988-marine-organisms-arsenic-speciation">Distribution of inorganic arsenic and methylated arsenic in marine organisms</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Applied Organometallic Chemistry</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/kaise1988-marine-organisms-arsenic-speciation">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

These are observational comparisons from single studies; the size of the difference depends on the site, metal and distance.

No source in the library converted oysters concentrations into a verified estimate of intake for a defined population. Concentrations describe the food, not individual risk.

<a id="what-remains-unresolved-when-was-each-answer-reviewed-and-what-changed-in-this-version"></a>

Every source record that names oysters was decided on its content: 29 occurrence extracted, 29 records in all. The occurrence table renders every extracted result; held values remain visible with their reason.

References identify the sources used in these answers. The Sources index preserves additional discovery links; inclusion there does not mean a source has been reviewed for this assessment. Corrections, completed searches, new direct evidence and changes in requirements should reopen the relevant answer.

## Oysters FAQs

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-oysters" data-anchor="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-oysters" data-question="What heavy metals are found in oysters?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>What heavy metals are found in oysters?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

The library reports lead, cadmium, total arsenic, inorganic arsenic, dimethylarsinic acid, monomethylarsonic acid, total mercury, methylmercury, nickel, chromium, aluminium, tin, antimony, Cu, Zn, V, Se, AsB, AsC, AsIII, AsV, DBT, DBT_as_Sn, DOT, DPhT, DPhT_as_Sn, MBT, MBT_as_Sn, MPhT, MPhT_as_Sn, OTC_sum_as_Sn, Sn_total_organotin, sumBT, sumOTC, sumPhT, TBT, TBT_as_Sn, TBT+DBT+TPhT, TMA, TPhT, TPhT_as_Sn and TPT in oysters, most often lead, cadmium and total arsenic.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span <details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-do-heavy-metals-get-into-oysters" data-anchor="how-do-heavy-metals-get-into-oysters" data-question="How do heavy metals get into oysters?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How do heavy metals get into oysters?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

In the studies available, oysters from contaminated or exposed settings carried more metal than oysters from the same study’s control.<sup class="cite">[[sources/kaise1988-marine-organisms-arsenic-speciation|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Kaise T, Hanaoka K, Tagawa S, Hirayama T, Fukui S · 1988</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/kaise1988-marine-organisms-arsenic-speciation">Distribution of inorganic arsenic and methylated arsenic in marine organisms</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Applied Organometallic Chemistry</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/kaise1988-marine-organisms-arsenic-speciation">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Oysters, as sold from water-soluble had TMA higher at 6,150 µg/kg, against 430 µg/kg for lipid-soluble in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/kaise1988-marine-organisms-arsenic-speciation|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Kaise T, Hanaoka K, Tagawa S, Hirayama T, Fukui S · 1988</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/kaise1988-marine-organisms-arsenic-speciation">Distribution of inorganic arsenic and methylated arsenic in marine organisms</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Applied Organometallic Chemistry</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/kaise1988-marine-organisms-arsenic-speciation">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-regions-report-the-lowest-levels-in-oysters" data-anchor="which-regions-report-the-lowest-levels-in-oysters" data-question="Which regions report the lowest levels in oysters?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which regions report the lowest levels in oysters?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Among GEMS/Food reporting regions, oysters, as sold had the lowest lead subgroup median in WPRO (13 µg/kg) and the highest in WPRO (205 µg/kg); reporting regions are markets, not growing areas.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> For cadmium, the lowest regional median was in WPRO (29.5 µg/kg) and the highest in WPRO (1,200 µg/kg).<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-oysters-is-inorganic" data-anchor="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-oysters-is-inorganic" data-question="How much of the arsenic in oysters is inorganic?">
